## repo-sync

Getting the repository the tool lives in, refreshing it, deciding when the compiled binary has been invalidated by what arrived, and knowing whether a newer release exists.

Governs: `internal/repo/**`

- only Go sources and module files invalidate the binary
- a repository with an uncommitted change reads as dirty, and a clean one does not
- a repository with no remote says so rather than failing
- `Head` returns the commit the repository is actually on
- **a repository with no commits gives `Head` an empty answer, not an error** — the one call that deliberately swallows a git failure, pinned so a later tidy-up cannot turn it into an error and break the empty-repository path in silence
- `ChangedSince` names the paths a commit touched and no others
- an empty revision means "nothing to compare against", not a diff against everything
- **`Pull` brings a commit across from a local bare remote** — no network, so the test cannot flake on one
- **`Pull` refuses a diverged history**, which is what `--ff-only` is for: a merge commit made by a background command is a merge commit nobody chose
- outside a repository the reads error rather than answering "clean" and "no remote"
- the highest plain semver wins, from real `ls-remote` output over annotated tags
- **a tag whose own `go.mod` retracts it is skipped** — the tombstone, offered as an update until it was not
- **a tag whose `go.mod` cannot be read is not offered either**, and the walk falls through to the next candidate rather than refusing outright
- every `retract` form is read: single, block, and an inclusive `[low, high]` range
- a remote whose only tags are prereleases has no release to offer, and that is not an error
- nor does a remote with no tags at all
- **a cancelled context stops the call** — an unanswering network must not hold the panel's first paint
- no remote configured cannot be asked
- ordering is numeric per field, so `v0.10.0` beats `v0.9.0`
- **only plain `vX.Y.Z` parses** — prereleases, `git describe` strings, build metadata and `dev` are all rejected rather than ranked
- **a binary that cannot say what it is is never told it is out of date**
- and neither side being parseable settles it
- the remote is asked once per TTL, not once per launch
- and asked again once the TTL expires
- **failure is cached too**, so an offline machine does not pay the timeout every launch
- no `.git` means ask without caching, not fail

## targets

What an installable destination is. One interface, four implementations, and a hard rule that nothing outside this package may assume where any of them lives.

Governs: `internal/target/**`

- a kind reports its own item shape, so no caller has to know it
- **the root honours `CLAUDE_HOME` and falls back to `~/.claude`**
- each accepted kind resolves to its directory
- an unknown kind is rejected rather than invented
- presence is reported honestly
- an unresolvable root yields empty directories rather than a bad path
- the project target roots at `<dir>/.claude` and accepts the same three kinds
- it reports configured only once its root exists
- an unrooted project is inert rather than resolving to `/.claude`
- each scope resolves to its own root
- **no two destinations share a root**, or isolation is a claim with nothing behind it
- an unknown scope falls back to global rather than to nothing
- the codex root honours `AGENTS_HOME` and falls back to `~/.agents`
- codex serves skills at `<root>/skills` and rejects agents and commands
- codex reports presence honestly
- the opencode root honours `OPENCODE_HOME` and falls back to `~/.config/opencode`
- **opencode serves skills, commands and agents, each at `<root>/<kind>`** — the plural the shared helper already emits, and one of the two names OpenCode globs for each
- **the agent transform drops `tools:` and `model:`, adds `mode: subagent` and the ownership marker, and leaves the prose body byte-identical** — the body is the prompt, so a changed byte is changed behaviour
- **the transform is deterministic**, or every scan reports drift and install rewrites forever. Frontmatter is emitted in encounter order, never from a Go map
- **transforming the transform's own output changes nothing** — no stacked marker, no second `mode:`
- **a source with no usable frontmatter is refused** rather than emitted, because OpenCode throws on a malformed agent instead of skipping it
- **`Transforms` answers per kind, and only opencode implements `Transformer`** — two questions, two methods. With only `Transform`, an error meant both "this failed" and "this kind is linked", and every skill and command in the opencode destination was classified as a conflict
- **every tool resolves in both scopes onto its own root, with the same accepted kinds in both scopes: skills for codex, all three for opencode**
